blocks.text: **The problem.** Given the `root` of a binary search tree and a value `val` that is **not already in the tree**, insert it and return the root of the resulting BST. Any valid BST is accepted, but the standard answer — and the one interviewers expect — adds the value as a new **leaf**.

blocks.alt: Inserting 5 into the tree 4, 2, 7, 1, 3. 5 is greater than 4 so go right to 7; 5 is less than 7 and 7 has no left child, so 5 becomes the left child of 7. No other node moves.

elements.text: val = 5: walk down, then attach to the empty spot
elements.originalText: val = 5: walk down, then attach to the empty spot

blocks.text: Search for `val` as if it were there. The search ends by stepping off the tree at an empty child — and that empty child is exactly where `val` belongs: every comparison on the way agreed it fits there. Attaching a leaf never disturbs the rest of the tree.
1. Recursion: return the new subtree root

Each call returns the root of its subtree after the insert. For an empty subtree that's the new node; otherwise it's the same node, with one child replaced by the result of the recursive call. This "return the subtree and re-attach it" shape comes back in delete, trim and many other BST problems.

blocks.caption: The new node is created where the walk runs out; each call re-attaches its child on the way back.

blocks.text: **Time O(h), space O(h)** for the call stack.
2. A loop that remembers the parent
**Time O(h), space O(1).** Same path, no call stack.

blocks.alt: Recursion: O(h) time, O(h) space. Loop: O(h) time, O(1) space.

items: **Empty tree** — the new node is the root.
**New smallest or largest value** — it goes at the far left or far right.
**A chain** — inserting at the end walks the whole chain: O(n).
**Returning the root** — forgetting to return it (or returning the new node) is the classic bug.
**Insert at the root** — insert as a leaf, then rotate it up; recently inserted values become fastest to find.
**Insert into a self-balancing tree** — insert as a leaf, then fix the balance on the way back up with rotations.
**Insert with duplicates** — decide where equal values go (or keep a count per node).
